title: Sharing in a ratio with the bar model
examples: How do you share 30 in the ratio 2:3?
How do I share money in a ratio?

explain.say: Amara and Chen win 30 dollars in a quiz. They share it in the ratio 2 to 3. How much does each get? First, add the parts: 2 plus 3 is 5. See the bar cut into 5 equal boxes?

draw.text: Sharing in a ratio with the bar model

explain.say: Next, share the 30 dollars into the 5 boxes. Watch them fill up. 30 divided by 5 is 6. So each box, each part, is worth 6 dollars. Can you check 5 times 6 is 30?
Amara has 2 parts. Look at her bar: 2 times 6 is 12 dollars. Now, how many parts does Chen have?

items.label: Amara 12 dollars
items.ask: How do you find one part?

items.label: Chen 18 dollars
items.ask: How do you check a ratio share?

explain.say: Chen has 3 parts, so 3 times 6 is 18 dollars. Check it: 12 plus 18 is 30. And 12 to 18 shrinks back to 2 to 3. It works!

items.label: Amara 12 dollars
items.ask: How do you find one part?

items.label: Chen 18 dollars
items.ask: How do you check a ratio share?

explain.say: Fantastic, you just used the bar model, a trick from Singapore maths books. Add the parts, find one part, multiply up. Challenge: share 40 mangoes in the ratio 3 to 5. Hint: there are 8 parts, so each part is 5.

faq.q: Why do you add the parts first?
faq.a: Adding the parts tells you how many equal boxes the whole amount is cut into. In 2 to 3 there are 5 boxes.
asks: Why add 2 and 3 when sharing in a ratio?

faq.q: How do you find one part?
faq.a: Divide the total by the number of parts. 30 dollars shared into 5 parts is 6 dollars per part.

faq.q: How do you check a ratio share?
faq.a: Add the shares to see they make the total, then simplify them to see they give the ratio. 12 plus 18 is 30, and 12 to 18 is 2 to 3.
asks: How do I know my ratio answer is right?

faq.q: How do you share 40 in the ratio 3 to 5?
faq.a: There are 8 parts, so one part is 40 divided by 8, which is 5. The shares are 3 times 5, which is 15, and 5 times 5, which is 25.

faq.q: What if I only know one share?
faq.a: Use it to find one part. If Chen has 3 parts worth 18 dollars, one part is 6, so Amara with 2 parts has 12.
asks: How do you work backwards in a ratio?

facts: When you share in a ratio, the number of equal parts is the sum of the numbers in the ratio.
The bar model, also called the model method, is a key part of Singapore primary maths.

quiz.say: Share 24 sweets in the ratio 1 to 3. How many go in the bigger share?
quiz.why: There are 4 parts, so one part is 6, and the bigger share is 3 parts, which is 18.

wrong.1: 8 divides 24 by 3 instead of by the 4 parts.
wrong.2: 6 is just one part, the smaller share.

quiz.say: Rosa and Ken share money in the ratio 2 to 5. Ken gets 35 dollars. How much does Rosa get?
quiz.why: Ken has 5 parts worth 35, so one part is 7, and Rosa has 2 parts, which is 14 dollars.

wrong.1: That would make the shares equal, not 2 to 5.
wrong.2: 7 dollars is only one part, and Rosa has two.
